Find CDC HIV-related service providers by ZIP code

Source: R/providers.R
cdc_providers.Rd

Queries the CDC Locator API to return service providers within a given radius of one or more ZIP codes.

Usage

cdc_providers(
  zipcode,
  radius = 10,
  services = NULL,
  client_id = NULL,
  client_token = NULL,
  distinct = TRUE,
  min_gap = NULL,
  progress = TRUE
)

Arguments

zipcode

One or more five-digit ZIP codes as strings, such as "02110". A number would lose leading zeros, so it is rejected.

radius

Search radius in miles: a whole number from 1 to 50. The default is 10.

services

Character vector of services to search for, matched in any case: "hivtesting", "stdtesting", "selftesting", "preptesting", "pep", "condom", "hepc", "doxypep", "mailintesting", "ryanwhite", "clinics", "substanceabuse", "mentalhealth" or "housing". NULL, the default, searches for all of them. More than three services take more than one request.

client_id

Optional CDC client ID override.

client_token

Optional CDC client token override.

distinct

With several ZIP codes, TRUE (the default) keeps each provider once, from the search where it was nearest. FALSE keeps one row for each ZIP code that found it.

min_gap

The least time between requests, in seconds, from 0.5 to 60. NULL, the default, means 0.5 for one ZIP code and 1 for several.

progress

With several ZIP codes, whether to show a progress bar (only in interactive sessions) and a one-line summary at the end.

Value

A tibble of service providers, with columns type, id, search_zipcode (the ZIP code whose search found the provider) and attributes. There is one row per provider record, or, for several ZIP codes with distinct = FALSE, one row per provider record and ZIP code that found it. Use cdc_providers_tidy() to flatten it.

Details

The API returns providers offering any of the requested services, but returned no providers when all 14 services were requested at once (observed 2026-11-16). So services are requested at most three at a time, and the results are combined: the default, every service, takes five requests per ZIP code. Providers returned by more than one request for the same ZIP code are kept once, by id.

Several ZIP codes

Give zipcode a vector to search around each ZIP code in turn. Every ZIP code is checked before any request is sent, and a repeated ZIP code is searched once. Nearby circles overlap, so with distinct = TRUE a provider found from more than one ZIP code is kept once, from the search where it was nearest; its distance and search_zipcode then belong together.

With one ZIP code, an error stops the call. With several, a ZIP code the API doesn't know (HTTP 500 "No point found for address") is skipped, the search carries on, and a warning lists the skipped ZIP codes at the end. They are also kept, with the API's message, in attr(result, "failures"); read it straight away, because most data-frame operations, including cdc_providers_tidy(), drop it. Any other error, such as a refused request (HTTP 403), a gateway error (502 or 504), any other HTTP 500 or a network failure, stops the call, because it could affect every remaining ZIP code.

Requests are spaced at least min_gap seconds apart: 0.5 seconds for one ZIP code and 1 second for several, unless you set it. A search of 30 ZIP codes for every service is 150 requests, about two and a half minutes. In an interactive session a progress bar shows how far the search has got. Pressing Esc stops the search and discards what was found so far, so for a long search it can help to search in smaller groups of ZIP codes.
